pool_config.pool_brief: Build a system that demonstrates asynchronous JavaScript patterns. Your solution must use: setTimeout for delayed execution, setInterval with clearInterval for repeated actions, demonstrate sync vs async execution order, implement a sequential callback pipeline (at least 3 steps nested), and log output that proves the execution order. All variables must use const or let.

projects.title: Publica Academy Class Notification System
projects.scenario: Build an automated class notification system for Publica Academy. Simulate a class starting countdown, timed reminders, and a sequential enrolment verification pipeline using async patterns.
requirements: Demonstrate execution order: log 3 sync statements and 2 async (setTimeout 0ms and 1000ms) to prove async runs after sync
Use setInterval to create a countdown from 5 to 0 (one tick per second); log each tick; clearInterval when it reaches 0 and log 'Class is now LIVE!'
Use setTimeout to schedule 3 notifications at different delays (500ms, 1200ms, 2000ms); each logs a different reminder message

Build a 4-step sequential callback pipeline: (1) verify student → (2) check seat availability → (3) process payment → (4) confirm enrolment. Each step uses setTimeout(callback, 600) to simulate async work and logs its step name on completion
After the pipeline completes (inside the final callback), log a summary message with the student name

projects.title: Paystack Payment Processing Pipeline
projects.scenario: Build a payment processing simulation for Paystack. Demonstrate async execution order, a transaction timeout monitor, staged notifications, and a sequential payment verification pipeline.
requirements: Demonstrate execution order: log 3 sync statements and 2 async (setTimeout 0ms and 1000ms) to prove async runs after sync
Use setInterval to simulate a transaction timeout monitor that logs 'Checking...' every second for 5 seconds, then clearInterval and log 'Transaction timeout reached'
Use setTimeout to schedule 3 payment status updates at different delays (400ms, 900ms, 1500ms); each logs a status message
Build a 4-step sequential callback pipeline: (1) validate card → (2) charge card → (3) verify with bank → (4) send receipt. Each step uses setTimeout(callback, 500) and logs on completion
After the pipeline completes, log a final success message with the transaction amount

projects.title: Bolt Ride Request Simulator
projects.scenario: Build a ride request simulation for Bolt. Demonstrate async execution order, a driver search interval, staged ride updates, and a sequential ride-matching pipeline using callbacks.
requirements: Demonstrate execution order: log 3 sync statements and 2 async (setTimeout 0ms and 1000ms) to prove async runs after sync
Use setInterval to simulate searching for nearby drivers — log 'Searching...' every second for 4 seconds, then clearInterval and log 'Driver found!'
Use setTimeout to schedule 3 ride status updates at different delays (600ms, 1200ms, 2000ms): 'Driver assigned', 'Driver en route', 'Driver arrived'
Build a 4-step sequential callback pipeline: (1) confirm pickup location → (2) match driver → (3) calculate fare → (4) start ride. Each step uses setTimeout(callback, 700) and logs on completion
After the pipeline completes, log a summary with the fare amount

projects.title: PiggyVest Auto-Save Scheduler
projects.scenario: Build an auto-save scheduling simulation for PiggyVest. Demonstrate async execution order, a recurring savings timer, staged deposit notifications, and a sequential savings verification pipeline.
requirements: Demonstrate execution order: log 3 sync statements and 2 async (setTimeout 0ms and 1000ms) to prove async runs after sync
Use setInterval to simulate an auto-save that logs 'Auto-saving ₦500...' every second for 5 cycles, then clearInterval and log total saved (₦2,500)
Use setTimeout to schedule 3 deposit confirmations at different delays (300ms, 800ms, 1500ms); each logs a confirmation with an amount
Build a 4-step sequential callback pipeline: (1) authenticate user → (2) check balance → (3) debit source → (4) credit savings. Each step uses setTimeout(callback, 600) and logs on completion
After the pipeline completes, log a final balance update message

projects.title: Jumia Order Fulfilment Tracker
projects.scenario: Build an order fulfilment tracking simulation for Jumia. Demonstrate async execution order, a delivery progress ticker, staged shipping notifications, and a sequential order processing pipeline.
requirements: Demonstrate execution order: log 3 sync statements and 2 async (setTimeout 0ms and 1000ms) to prove async runs after sync
Use setInterval to simulate delivery progress — log 'Checkpoint N reached' every second for 4 checkpoints, then clearInterval and log 'Package delivered!'
Use setTimeout to schedule 3 shipping notifications at different delays (500ms, 1000ms, 1800ms): 'Order confirmed', 'Shipped', 'Out for delivery'
Build a 4-step sequential callback pipeline: (1) verify order → (2) pick from warehouse → (3) hand to courier → (4) confirm delivery. Each step uses setTimeout(callback, 500) and logs on completion
After the pipeline completes, log a delivery summary with the order ID

descriptors.full: Correctly demonstrates that sync code runs before async; setTimeout(fn, 0) runs after all sync code; output clearly shows the order with labelled logs
descriptors.partial: Attempt made but order not clearly demonstrated or labels missing

descriptors.full: setInterval correctly counts or repeats an action; clearInterval stops it at the right time; multiple setTimeout calls fire at correct relative delays; interval ID stored in a variable
descriptors.partial: setInterval used but clearInterval missing or incorrect; or setTimeout used but only one call

descriptors.full: 4+ steps nested correctly; each step executes only after the previous completes; output proves sequential order; final callback logs a summary
descriptors.partial: Pipeline attempted but fewer than 4 steps, or steps not properly nested (parallel instead of sequential)
descriptors.none: No callback nesting; steps run independently

descriptors.full: const/let used; logs are labelled and clear; timer IDs stored properly; no var; code is readable
descriptors.partial: Minor issues — unlabelled logs or missing timer ID variable
descriptors.none: var used, unreadable output, or timers leak (no clearInterval)
